Daily Quiz.question: ১) Which of the following is a prominent character of the novel “Wuthering Heights”?
Daily Quiz.exp:
• Wuthering Heights is a famous novel which is written by Emily Bronte.
• The important character of this novel:
- Heathcliff
- Catherine
- Edgar Linton
- Nelly Dean
- Isabella Linton
- Lockwood

Source: SparksNote

Daily Quiz.question: ২) Victorian period started in-
Daily Quiz.exp:
English Literature Periods:
450 - 1066 :- The Old English Period
1066 - 1500 :- The Middle English Period
1500 - 1660 :- The Renaissance Period
1660 - 1785 :- The Neoclassical Period
1798 - 1832 :- Romantic Period
1832 - 1901 :- Victorian Period

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৩) 'On Liberty' is written by-
Daily Quiz.exp:
John Stuart Mill (1806-73): English philosopher, economist, and exponent of utilitarianism.
Works:
- On Liberty
- Utilitarianism
- The Subjection of Women
- A System of Logic

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman; britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) Who is the author of 'The Descent of Man'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Charles Robert Darwin: English naturalist whose scientific theory of evolution by natural selection became the foundation of modern evolutionary studies.

Works:
- The Origin of the Species
- The Descent of Man etc.

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ৫) Who wrote the famous elegy ''In Memoriam''?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Lord Alfred Tennyson: English poet often regarded as the chief representative of the Victorian age in poetry.
- His famous elegy is ''In Memoriam''.

His other famous poems:
- Oenone,
- Ulysses,
- Lotos Eaters,
- Locksley Hall,
- Tears, Idle Tears,
- Tithonus,
- The Lady of Shalott,
- Vision of Sin,
- Morte D'Arthur etc.

Famous play:
- The Falcon,
- Queen Mary,
- Harold.

Source: Poetry Foundation

Daily Quiz.question: ৬) 'Vanity Fair' is a famous ____ by William Makepeace Thackeray.
Daily Quiz.exp:
William Makepeace Thackeray: English novelist whose reputation rests chiefly on Vanity Fair (1847–48), a novel of the Napoleonic period in England.

Other works:
- The History of Henry Esmond, Esq
- The Virginians
- Pendennis
- The Newcomes
- The Rose and the Ring
- Barry Lyndon

Source: britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ৭) 'Oliver Twist' is a famous novel of -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Charles Dickens: English novelist, generally considered the greatest of the Victorian era.

Famous novel of Charles Dickens:
- Oliver Twist,
- A Tale of Two Cities,
- Great Expectations,
- David Copperfield,
- The Christmas Carol,
- The Bleak House,
- The Battle of Life etc.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Encyclopedia Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ৮) The background of the novel 'A Tale of Two Cities' is-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- A Tale of Two Cities is a novel by Charles Dickens that was first published in 1859.
- The story is set in the late 18th century against the background of the French Revolution.

Some important characters from this novel:
- Charles Darnay
- Sydney Carton
- Doctor Manette
- Madame Defarge
- Lucie Manette
- Jarvis Lorry
- Monsieur Ernest Defarge

Source: sparknotes and britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) 'The Ring and the Book' is a -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Robert Browning: Major English poet of the Victorian age, noted for his mastery of dramatic monologue and psychological portraiture.
- His most noted work was The Ring and the Book (1868–69), more than 20,000-line poem written in blank verse and published in 12 books from 1868 to 1869, the story of a Roman murder trial in 12 books.

Among Browning’s other important publications are:
- Pauline (1833),
- Bells and Pomegranates (1841–46),
- My Last Duchess,
- Men and Women (1855),
- Dramatis Personae (1864), 
- Asolando (1889).

Source: britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) 'Jane Eyre' is a famous work of -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Charlotte Bronte is a Victorian novelist.

Famous Works:
- Jane Eyre,
- Shirley,
- Villette,
- The Professor etc.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১১) Which of the following books is written by Karl Marx?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Karl Marx: Revolutionary, sociologist, historian, and economist.

His famous books are:
- Das Kapital,
- Communist Manifesto,
- Holy Family,
- The Poverty of Philosophy.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Encyclopedia of Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ১২) George Eliot's real name is -
Daily Quiz.exp:
George Eliot: Her real name is Mary Ann Evans.

Famous Works:
- The Mill on the Floss,
- Scenes of Clerical Life,
- Adam Bede,
- Silas Marner,
- Romola,
- Middlemarch.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১৩) Who is the author of the novel 'Moby Dick'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Herman Melville was an American Novelist, short-story writer and poet.

His famous novels are:
- Moby Dick,
- White Jacket,
- Bartleby, the Scrivener.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৪) Who is the author of 'Culture and Anarchy'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Matthew Aronld (1822-88):
He was a poet and a critic, known for his strong moral voice.
Works:
- “Essays in Criticism” (1888)
- Culture and Anarchy (1867) and some poems.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১৫) Who wrote 'Life on the Mississippi'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Mark Twain, pseudonym of Samuel Langhorne Clemens: American humorist, journalist, lecturer, and novelist who acquired international fame for his travel narratives, especially:

- The Innocents Abroad (1869),
- Roughing It (1872), and
- Life on the Mississippi (1883),

and for his adventure stories of boyhood, especially:
- The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (1876) and
- Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1885).

Source: britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) Who is the author of ''The Return of the Native''?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Thomas Hardy: One of the most renowned poets and regional novelists in English literary history.

His famous novels:
- Tess of the d'urbervilles,
- Far from the madding crowd,
- The Return of the Native,
- The Poor Man and the Lady,
- The Mayor of Casterbridge,
- Jude the Obscure,
- A Pair of Blue Eyes.

Source: britannica and poetry foundation

Daily Quiz.question: ১৭) 'The Portrait of a Lady' is written by which of the following writers?
Daily Quiz.exp:
সঠিক উত্তর - খ) Henry James
Henry James (1843-1916): He is an American English writer.

His novels:
- Daisy Miller,
- The Portrait of a Lady,
- The Bostonians,
- The Ambassadors,
- The Wings of the Dove, 
- The American,
- The Tragic Muse,
- The Spoils of Poyton.

Source: An ABC of English Literature and Live MCQ lecture; Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৮) Which one is the central character of 'Man and Superman'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
- The prolific Irish playwright George Bernard Shaw first wrote Man and Superman in 1903.
- The play centers on Ann Whitefield, a graceful and intelligent young woman.

Other important characters are:
- Roebuck Ramsden,
- Jack Tanner,
- Actavius Robinson.

Source: CliffsNotes and SparkNotes

Daily Quiz.question: ১৯) 'Ignorance is not innocence but sin' —quoted by-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Robert Browning: Major English poet of the Victorian age, noted for his mastery of dramatic monologue and psychological portraiture.

His famous quotes:
- Ignorance is not innocence but sin.
- So absolutely good is truth, truth never hurts the teller.

Among Browning’s important publications are:
- The Ring and the Book (1868–69),
- Pauline (1833),
- Bells and Pomegranates (1841–46),
- My Last Duchess,
- Men and Women (1855),
- Dramatis Personae (1864), 
- Asolando (1889).

Source: britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ২০) 'Life isn't about finding yourself. Life is about creating yourself' is a famous quotation by-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Some famous quote of G. B. Shaw:
- “Success does not consist in never making mistakes but in never making the same one a second time.”
- “Life isn't about finding yourself. Life is about creating yourself.”
- “The reasonable man adapts himself to the world: the unreasonable one persists in trying to adapt the world to himself. Therefore all progress depends on the unreasonable man.”
- “There are two tragedies in life. One is to lose your heart's desire. The other is to gain it.”

Source: goodreads
